correctness.rationale: The exchange metric d(A,B)=r-|A∩B| is proved by monotonicity of intersection along each edge and an exchange path; diameter is r since n>=2r. Three-variable formulas define exact distance recursively. The p-pebble upper bound maintains every nonzero Venn-cell size of at most p held r-subsets; after lifting one pebble at most (p-1)r ground elements remain occupied, and both universes of size >=pr retain at least r fresh points, allowing every extension. For the lower bound, j pairwise disjoint r-sets plus a last r-set intersecting only the first in r-i points have union exactly jr+i, so for every t in (2r,pr] a sentence with j+1<=p variables detects n>=t. Distinct normalized ranks are detected by diameter. The finite checks independently corroborate both bounds; they do not prove the general case.

originality.rationale: The mathematical novelty is exact higher-width p>=4 classification for normalized ranks r>=3, not previous 3-variable or triangular-graph results. Earlier distance-regular FO^3 support characterizations imply the p=3 Johnson instance, and earlier triangular-graph width theorems imply only rank r=2. Neither implies p>=4 at r>=3: the exact ordered multiway Venn-cell extension strategy is new to this claim. Chepoi analyzes embeddings/metric structure, Grohe-Otto general game equivalences, the merged-Johnson literature automorphisms/orbitals, and Adler et al. the VC complexity of adjacency; inspected materials do not state the pr threshold. Relevant published-finding corpus searches returned no exact covering item. Residual priority risk from a stronger unnamed general set-system interpretation theorem remains. Prior specialized statements on one-dimensional counting refinement for arbitrarily many named Johnson vertices give stabilizer-orbit partitions, not plain higher-width first-order theory equivalence or the cutoff pr.

value.rationale: Sharp uniform cutoff pr for every width p>=4 and normalized rank r>=3 gives a natural exact logical resource invariant for uniform matroid basis graphs. It distinguishes orders within the previously collapsed 3-variable stable class, provides arbitrarily high strict variable-width levels even at fixed r, and yields exact within-family theory counts and canonical smallest stable representatives of size binomial(pr,r). These facts address expressiveness and finite-model equivalence, not an arbitrary numerical slice or routine table recomputation.
